analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is the most common sexually transmitted infection and a principal cause of cervical cancer, yet comprehensive and updated data on HPV prevalence and genotype distribution in Isfahan, central Iran, remain limited despite regional reports.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective study analyzed HPV PCR and genotyping results from 4,973 women screened between 2015 and 2024 at a referral laboratory in Isfahan, central Iran.
analysis_en.methods: The study collected and analyzed HPV PCR and genotyping results alongside available demographic data from women referred for genital HPV screening.
analysis_en.main_results: Of 4,973 women screened, 819 (16.5%) tested HPV-positive, with HPV6 being the most common genotype (9.2%). Among HPV-positive women, high-risk types were slightly more frequent than low-risk types (55.2% vs. 44.8%), with HPV16 (14.4%) the most prevalent high-risk genotype, followed by HPV53 (13.2%) and HPV18 (6.2%). HPV positivity was highest in women under 20 years of age (27.3%; P = 0.002).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the high HPV infection rate in Isfahan as comparable to other regions in Iran and noted that more than half of HPV-positive women were infected with high-risk types, highlighting the burden of oncogenic HPV in the population.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest a substantial burden of HPV infection and high-risk genotypes in Isfahan, which may inform local vaccination strategies and cervical cancer screening programs.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design and reliance on a single referral laboratory limit generalizability, and the absence of clinical outcomes or longitudinal follow-up reduces the strength of evidence for causal inference.

title_zh: 2015年至2024年伊朗中部伊斯法罕女性人乳头瘤病毒类型患病率的回顾性研究
source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes the most prevalent sexually transmitted infection and is the principal cause of cervical cancer. Despite several regional reports from Iran, comprehensive and updated data on HPV prevalence and genotype distribution among women in Isfahan, central Iran, remain limited. The present study aimed to determine the prevalence of HPV infection and HPV types in the recordings of women referred for genital HPV screening to a Medical Laboratory in Isfahan, central Iran. In this retrospective study, HPV PCR and genotyping results of 4,973 women and their available demographic data screened between 2015 and 2024 at a referral laboratory in Isfahan were collected, analyzed and reported. Of 4,973 women screened, 819 (16.5%) tested HPV-positive. HPV6 was the most common genotype (9.2%). Among HPV-positive women, high-risk types were slightly more frequent than low-risk types (55.2% vs. 44.8%), with HPV16 (14.4%) the most prevalent high-risk genotype, followed by HPV53 (13.2%) and HPV18 (6.2%). HPV positivity was highest in women under 20 years of age (27.3%; P = 0.002). Based on the results of the present study, the rate of HPV infection in Isfahan was high, yet comparable to that reported in several other regions in Iran. More than half of HPV-positive women were infected with high-risk types in Isfahan area. Among the tested population, the highest positivity was observed in women under 20 years old.
abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 引起最流行的性传播感染,也是 宫颈癌 的主要原因。尽管伊朗发布了几份区域报告,但有关伊朗中部伊斯法罕妇女中 HPV 患病率 和基因型分布的全面和最新数据仍然有限。本研究旨在确定转介至伊朗中部伊斯法罕医学实验室进行生殖器 HPV 筛查的女性记录中 HPV 感染的 患病率 和 HPV 类型。在这项回顾性研究中,收集、分析和报告了 2015 年至 2024 年间在伊斯法罕转诊实验室筛查的 4,973 名女性的 HPV PCR 和基因分型结果及其可用的人口统计数据。在接受筛查的 4,973 名女性中,819 名 (16.5%) 检测出 HPV 呈阳性。HPV6 是最常见的基因型(9.2%)。在HPV阳性女性中,高危型的发生率略高于低危型(55.2% vs. 44.8%),其中HPV16(14.4%)是最常见的高危基因型,其次是HPV53(13.2%)和HPV18(6.2%)。20 岁以下女性的 HPV 阳性率最高(27.3%;P = 0.002)。根据本研究的结果,伊斯法罕的 HPV 感染率很高,但与伊朗其他几个地区报告的情况相当。在伊斯法罕地区,超过一半的HPV阳性女性感染了高危型。在受测人群中,20岁以下的女性阳性率最高。

title: Correlation between high-risk Human Papillomavirus (HPV) viral load and cervical lesions across different subtypes, along with the development of a clinical prediction model
abstract: Abstract Objective The study aims to investigate the correlation between the viral loads of HPV16/18 and 16 other high-risk HPV types (designated as non-16/18 group) and the severity of cervical lesions, and to develop a HSIL+ risk prediction model to furnish evidence for pragmatic clinical triage and precision management strategies. Methods A retrospective analysis was performed on the data from 331 HR-HPV-positive patients collected between July 2025 and January 2026. Using a semi-quantitative hybrid capture-chemiluminescence platform,The viral loads of HPV16/18 and non-16/18 group were measured, and patients were categorized into normal, LSIL, HSIL, and cervical cancer groups based on pathological findings. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was employed to examine the associations among viral load, HPV subtypes, age, and lesion severity, and a HSIL+ prediction nomogram was constructed. Results The prevalence of HPV16/18 infection escalated with increasing lesion severity (HSIL: OR=6.50; cervical cancer: OR=23.28), demonstrating a pattern of “continuous augmentation”. Conversely, the viral load of non-16/18 group increased during the LSIL and HSIL stages but declined in the cancer stage, exhibiting a pattern of “early involvement followed by later attenuation”. While single non-16/18 group infections demonstrated early warning value, HPV16/18 types and medium to high viral loads were identified as independent risk factors for HSIL+. The nomogram underwent Bootstrap validation and yielded an AUC of 0.763, indicating satisfactory calibration. Conclusion This study comprehensively analyzed the pathogenic features of viral loads associated with HPV16/18 and other high-risk subtypes, elucidating the lesion patterns of distinct subtypes. While HPV16/18 acts as the principal persistent driver, the high viral load of the non-16/18 group provides a critical "window-of-opportunity" indication during the precancerous phase. A pragmatic HSIL+ risk-stratification nomogram was devised to serve as an accessible clinical aid for the early identification of high-risk lesions, thereby optimizing real-world personalized management.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomaviruses (HPV), particularly HPV16/18, is a principal driver of cervical carcinogenesis, yet the relationship between viral load and lesion severity across HPV subtypes remains incompletely defined. The study sought to quantify this association and to derive a clinical tool to guide triage of HPV-positive patients.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 331 high-risk HPV-positive patients whose data were collected between July 2025 and January 2026. Patients were stratified by HPV subtype (HPV16/18 versus 16 other high-risk types) and by cervical lesion severity into normal, LSIL, HSIL, and cervical cancer groups.
analysis.methods: Viral loads for HPV16/18 and the non-16/18 group were measured using a semi-quantitative hybrid capture–chemiluminescence platform. Multivariate logistic regression was used to assess associations among viral load, HPV subtype, age, and lesion severity, and a HSIL+ risk prediction nomogram was constructed and validated by bootstrap.
analysis.main_results: HPV16/18 infection prevalence increased with lesion severity (HSIL: OR=6.50; cervical cancer: OR=23.28), while non-16/18 viral load rose during LSIL and HSIL but declined in cancer. HPV16/18 types and medium-to-high viral loads were identified as independent risk factors for HSIL+, and the nomogram achieved an AUC of 0.763.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret HPV16/18 as the principal persistent driver of progression, whereas high non-16/18 viral load signals a critical precancerous window. They report a novel HSIL+ risk-stratification nomogram that integrates subtype-specific viral load and age for pragmatic clinical triage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support subtype-aware, viral-load–based triage to prioritize high-risk HPV-positive patients for early colposcopy or intervention, potentially reducing overtreatment and improving resource allocation in cervical cancer prevention programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design, single-center sampling, and reliance on semi-quantitative viral load measurement limit causal inference and generalizability; bootstrap validation yielded moderate discrimination (AUC 0.763), indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study of 331 high-risk HPV-positive patients collected between July 2025 and January 2026 examined how viral loads of HPV16/18 and 16 other high-risk types correlate with cervical lesion severity. title: Immunological and antitumor responses to HPV-targeted therapeutic vaccines in preclinical models of head and neck cancer: a systematic review.
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is increasingly prevalent and accounts for 22-70% of HNSCCs depending on the region. Although prophylactic HPV vaccines were approved in the early 2000s to prevent HPV infection and oncogenesis, they are ineffective against established HPV infections and related cancers. The standard of care for these HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancers combines radiotherapy, surgery, and chemotherapy. However, these treatments can result in significant lifelong side effects for patients with no new treatments entering regular clinical practice in the past decade. Therapeutic cancer vaccines represent an opportunity for novel treatment approaches in HPV-associated cancer, particularly because these cancers display viral tumor-specific antigens (TSAs) such as E6 and E7, making them easily targetable by this type of immunotherapy. Currently, there are no FDA-approved therapeutic vaccines for HPV-associated cancers, but preclinical and clinical studies are ongoing in this area. In this systematic review, we describe current HPV vaccination strategies, their biological mechanisms, and their immunological and therapeutic effects in preclinical cancer models. We discuss each component of therapeutic vaccines: antigens, delivery platforms, adjuvants, and combination agents. We also assess the results of recent preclinical studies evaluating HPV therapeutic vaccines to provide an outlook on the future of this treatment modality.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述将 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 相关头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC) 作为目标病原体和疾病,重点关注临床前模型中的治疗 疫苗。核心问题涉及 HPV 相关 HNSCC 临床前研究中 HPV 靶向治疗药物 疫苗 引起的免疫和抗肿瘤反应。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇系统综述,综合了 HPV 治疗药物 疫苗 的临床前研究,详细介绍了 疫苗 的组成部分(抗原、递送平台、佐剂和组合药物),并评估了临床前癌症模型中的免疫学和治疗效果。该综述明确将其范围界定为描述当前的 HPV 疫苗接种 策略及其在临床前背景下的生物学机制。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该审查强调,HPV 相关的 HNSCC 是一种重大的疾病负担,根据地区的不同,HPV 占 HNSCC 的 22-70%。它强调治疗性 疫苗 利用病毒肿瘤特异性抗原,例如 E6 和 E7,这些抗原很容易被 HPV 相关癌症的免疫疗法靶向。此外,该审查指出,尽管正在进行临床前和临床研究,但 FDA 尚未批准用于 HPV 相关癌症的治疗药物 疫苗。

title: Improving cervical cancer screening uptake through theory-informed education: a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: This study examined whether theory-based education increases cervical cancer screening among underserved women. METHODS: Seven databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) were systematically searched for studies published between January 2005 and November 2025. A total of 1,200 records were identified; after duplicate removal, 900 titles and abstracts were screened, and 200 full-text articles were assessed. Fourteen studies met inclusion criteria for qualitative synthesis, and 12 trials contributed extractable binary outcome data for meta-analysis, including one study with two distinct intervention arms. The primary outcome was screening uptake (Pap smear, visual inspection with acetic acid [VIA], or human papillomavirus [HPV] testing). Data extraction and quality appraisal followed PRISMA 2020 and Joanna Briggs Institute guidance. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) were calculated using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, and heterogeneity, prediction intervals, small-study effects, and certainty of evidence (GRADE) were evaluated. RESULTS: Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care or minimal information (OR = 4.41; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.21-8.80). Subgroup analyses showed substantial effects in both high-income (OR = 3.46; 95% CI: 1.43-8.36) and middle-income settings (OR = 6.55; 95% CI: 2.74-15.63). Interventions frequently incorporated behavioral frameworks, such as the Health Belief Model, Protection Motivation Theory, and BASNEF model, and were often culturally tailored or delivered through community-embedded formats. INTERPRETATION: Integrating such interventions into national and local screening programs represents an effective and equitable strategy to reduce disparities in cervical cancer prevention.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines whether theory-informed educational interventions increase uptake of cervical cancer screening among underserved women, focusing on human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical cancer prevention and screening modalities such as Pap smear, VIA, or HPV testing.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that searched seven databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) for studies published between January 2005 and November 2025, identifying 1,200 records, screening 900 titles and abstracts, and assessing 200 full-text articles; 14 studies were included in qualitative synthesis and 12 trials contributed data for meta-analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care or minimal information (pooled OR = 4.41; 95% CI: 2.21–8.80), with substantial effects observed in both high-income (OR = 3.46; 95% CI: 1.43–8.36) and middle-income settings (OR = 6.55; 95% CI: 2.74–15.63).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review did not report on the long-term sustainability of intervention effects, differential impacts across specific underserved subgroups, or the cost-effectiveness of theory-informed education programs.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated whether theory-informed educational interventions improve cervical cancer screening uptake among underserved women. Using a comprehensive search across seven databases from 2005 to 2025, 14 studies were synthesized qualitatively and 12 trials were included in a meta-analysis. Structured educational interventions significantly increased screening uptake (pooled OR = 4.41; 95% CI: 2.21–8.80), with notable effects in both high-income and middle-income settings. Interventions frequently incorporated behavioral frameworks such as the Health Belief Model and were often culturally tailored or community-embedded. title: Strengthening Adolescent Sexual Health Literacy through Targeted Educational Interventions in German Secondary Schools.
abstract: Adolescents are a key population in STI prevention, yet many lack foundational knowledge and access to reliable information. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of a targeted sexual health education lecture on knowledge about STIs and HPV vaccination as well as behavioral intentions in Bavaria, Germany. We conducted a prospective, anonymized survey with students from secondary schools across Bavaria. An online questionnaire was completed before (t = 1; n = 5,988) and after (t = 2; n = 4,739) a standardized, extracurricular sexual health lecture. Participants were aged 14-20 years (mean age 16.1), from diverse school types. Key outcomes included self-assessed knowledge, ability to explain specific STIs, awareness of the HPV vaccine, and willingness to receive the vaccination. Self-reported STI knowledge increased significantly: only 29.1% of students felt well-informed at baseline, compared to 85.96% after the lecture. The average number of STIs students could explain rose from 1.91 to 6.49 (p < 0.001). HIV/AIDS was the most well-understood STI pre-intervention (69.9%), rising to 89.3% post-intervention. Uncertainty about STI transmission decreased from 20.3% to 5.0%. HPV vaccine awareness increased from 75.1% to 95.3%. Among those not vaccinated, willingness to receive the vaccine significantly improved (mean score 2.95 to 3.53 on a 5-point scale, p < 0.001). A single, structured sexual health lecture significantly improved adolescent knowledge of STIs, reduced misinformation, and increased willingness to engage in preventive behaviors, including HPV vaccination. These findings support integrating educational interventions into broader public health strategies targeting youth to reduce long-term infection risks and promote informed decision-making.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论描述了一项针对巴伐利亚中学生进行的前瞻性匿名调查。在标准化课外性健康讲座之前(n = 5,988)和之后(n = 4,739)进行了在线调查问卷。参与者年龄为 14-20 岁(平均年龄 16.1 岁),代表不同类型的学校。主要结果包括自我评估的性传播感染知识、解释特定性传播感染的能力、对 HPV 疫苗 的认识以及接受 疫苗接种 的意愿。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查建议将结构化的性健康教育讲座纳入针对青少年的公共卫生战略,以降低感染风险并促进知情决策。未来的研究应评估此类干预措施的长期影响,并探索解决服务不足人群知识差距的策略。

title: mRNA Vaccines Targeting HPV E6/E7: A New Frontier in Cervical Cancer Immunotherapy.
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infections, particularly high-risk types 16 and 18, are responsible for approximately 70% of cervical cancer cases worldwide. Despite the availability of effective prophylactic vaccines, therapeutic interventions for established HPV-associated malignancies remain limited. This mini-review synthesizes recent advances (2020-2026) in mRNA-LNP vaccine development targeting the HPV E6 and E7 oncoproteins. We examine the mechanistic basis for targeting E6/E7, technological advantages of mRNA-LNP platforms, and key preclinical evidence demonstrating potent T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity. Recent clinical progress, including BioNTech's BNT113 vaccine which received FDA Fast Track designation for HPV16-positive head and neck cancer, is discussed alongside ongoing challenges in delivery optimization, tumor microenvironment immunosuppression, and manufacturing scalability. The review concludes with future perspectives on combination strategies with immune checkpoint inhibitors and the potential for personalized neoantigen approaches.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇小型综述综合了 2020 年至 2026 年针对 HPV E6/E7 的 mRNA-LNP 疫苗 开发进展。它包括对 mRNA-LNP 平台的机制基础、技术优势、临床前证据和临床进展的讨论,例如 BioNTech 的 BNT113 疫苗 获得 FDA 快速通道指定,用于治疗 HPV16 阳性头颈癌。

title: Liquid Biopsy in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Systematic Review of the Scientific Literature.
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) presents a significant global health challenge, characterized by late-stage diagnosis and high rates of locoregional recurrence. Traditional tissue biopsy, while considered the gold standard, is invasive and often fails to capture the spatial and temporal heterogeneity of the tumor. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a transformative, noninvasive paradigm for molecular diagnostics, leveraging circulating biomarkers found in blood and saliva. This systematic review critically evaluates current evidence regarding the diagnostic accuracy, prognostic value, and molecular validity of circulating tumor cells, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and the transcriptomic landscape of coding and noncoding RNAs (miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs) in HNSCC. Our review highlights the specificity of ctDNA for monitoring minimal residual disease, particularly in human papillomavirus- and Epstein-Barr virus-driven malignancies, where viral kinetics serve as sensitive biomarkers for recurrence. Furthermore, we explore the utility of "Saliva-Exosomics," suggesting that salivary exosomes may offer high sensitivity for early-stage oral cavity lesions due to anatomical proximity. The review also synthesizes data on novel RNA species, such as tumor-educated platelets and circular RNAs, which act as stable systemic biosensors. Despite promising results, significant heterogeneity in isolation protocols and detection platforms (e.g., next-generation sequencing vs. digital PCR) remains a barrier to widespread clinical implementation. We conclude that integrating multianalyte liquid biopsies into clinical practice holds the potential to personalize therapeutic strategies, improve survival outcomes, and redefine the standard of care in head and neck oncology.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of liquid biopsy biomarkers—circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells, and RNA species (miRNAs, lncRNAs, circRNAs)—in human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), focusing on diagnostic accuracy, prognostic value, and molecular validity for HPV-driven malignancies.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic review evaluates evidence on circulating biomarkers in HNSCC, including ctDNA, circulating tumor cells, and RNA species (miRNAs, lncRNAs, circRNAs), with a focus on HPV- and Epstein-Barr virus-driven malignancies. The review synthesizes data on diagnostic accuracy, prognostic value, and molecular validity but does not report databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, or included-study counts.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: ctDNA demonstrates specificity for monitoring minimal residual disease in HPV-driven HNSCC, where viral kinetics serve as sensitive biomarkers for recurrence. Salivary exosomes show high sensitivity for early-stage oral cavity lesions due to anatomical proximity. Novel RNA species, such as tumor-educated platelets and circular RNAs, function as stable systemic biosensors in HNSCC.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Significant heterogeneity exists in isolation protocols and detection platforms (e.g., next-generation sequencing vs. digital PCR), which hinders widespread clinical implementation. The review does not report standardized protocols or comparative performance metrics across platforms.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Integrating multianalyte liquid biopsies into clinical practice may personalize therapeutic strategies and improve survival outcomes in HPV-associated HNSCC. Further research is needed to standardize isolation protocols and detection platforms to enable clinical translation.

title_zh: 头颈鳞状细胞癌的液体活检:科学文献的系统回顾。
source_body_en: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) presents a significant global health challenge, characterized by late-stage diagnosis and high rates of locoregional recurrence. Traditional tissue biopsy, while considered the gold standard, is invasive and often fails to capture the spatial and temporal heterogeneity of the tumor. Liquid biopsy has emerged as a transformative, noninvasive paradigm for molecular diagnostics, leveraging circulating biomarkers found in blood and saliva. This systematic review critically evaluates current evidence regarding the diagnostic accuracy, prognostic value, and molecular validity of circulating tumor cells, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and the transcriptomic landscape of coding and noncoding RNAs (miRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs) in HNSCC. Our review highlights the specificity of ctDNA for monitoring minimal residual disease, particularly in human papillomavirus- and Epstein-Barr virus-driven malignancies, where viral kinetics serve as sensitive biomarkers for recurrence. Furthermore, we explore the utility of "Saliva-Exosomics," suggesting that salivary exosomes may offer high sensitivity for early-stage oral cavity lesions due to anatomical proximity. The review also synthesizes data on novel RNA species, such as tumor-educated platelets and circular RNAs, which act as stable systemic biosensors. Despite promising results, significant heterogeneity in isolation protocols and detection platforms (e.g., next-generation sequencing vs. digital PCR) remains a barrier to widespread clinical implementation. We conclude that integrating multianalyte liquid biopsies into clinical practice holds the potential to personalize therapeutic strategies, improve survival outcomes, and redefine the standard of care in head and neck oncology.
abstract_zh: 头颈鳞状细胞癌 (HNSCC) 是一项重大的全球健康挑战,其特点是晚期 诊断 和高局部区域复发率。传统的组织活检虽然被认为是金标准,但具有侵入性,通常无法捕获肿瘤的空间和时间异质性。液体活检已成为一种革命性的、无创的分子诊断范例,利用血液和唾液中发现的循环生物标志物。本系统综述严格评估了有关 HNSCC 中循环肿瘤细胞、循环肿瘤 DNA (ctDNA) 以及编码和非编码 RNA(miRNA、lncRNA 和 circRNA)转录组学景观的诊断准确性、预后价值和分子有效性的当前证据。我们的综述强调了 ctDNA 在监测微小残留病方面的特异性,特别是在 人乳头瘤病毒 和 Epstein-Barr 病毒驱动的恶性肿瘤中,其中病毒动力学可作为复发的敏感生物标志物。此外,我们探索了“唾液外泌体”的实用性,表明唾液外泌体由于解剖学上的接近性可能对早期口腔病变具有高敏感性。该综述还综合了新型 RNA 种类的数据,例如肿瘤培养的血小板和环状 RNA,它们可作为稳定的全身生物传感器。尽管结果有希望,但分离方案和检测平台(例如下一代测序与数字 PCR)的显着异质性仍然是广泛临床实施的障碍。我们的结论是,将多分析物液体活检纳入临床实践有可能实现个性化治疗策略、改善生存结果并重新定义头颈肿瘤学的护理标准。

title: Addressing HPV vaccine hesitancy and misinformation in India through public health communication strategies.
abstract: ABSTRACT India witnessed a significant step forward in cervical cancer prevention and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage with the rollout of a nationwide free HPV vaccination drive aimed at vaccinating 14‐y‐old girls. However, the campaign’s success rate can be significantly reduced if timely measures to tackle vaccine hesitancy and related misinformation are not taken into account. This commentary article discusses the effects of HPV vaccine misinformation, identifies global vaccine hesitancy factors, and highlights behavioral determinants affecting HPV vaccine hesitancy and its coverage in India. It identifies low awareness, misconceptions, sociocultural beliefs, stigma, safety concerns, weak injunctive norms, parental resistance, urban–rural disparities, and health system barriers as key challenges associated with vaccine hesitancy and low vaccine uptake among adolescents in India. Using an integrated Health Belief Model (HBM) and COM-B theoretical framework, it proposes a culturally sensitive, evidence-based multifactorial communication strategy focused on raising awareness, building trust, countering misinformation, capacity building of healthcare providers, and enhancing opportunities for the adoption of HPV preventive behavior. The commentary highlights the need to actively engage parents, adolescents, healthcare providers, educators, influencers, media, and community members to strengthen vaccine confidence, social norms, and support India’s broader cervical cancer prevention goals in alignment with WHO’s 90–70–90 targets by 2030.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本评论讨论了印度对 HPV 疫苗 犹豫不决和错误信息的挑战,强调需要制定有针对性的公共卫生传播策略,以提高 疫苗 覆盖率和 宫颈癌 预防。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是对印度全国免费 HPV 疫苗接种 活动的评论性分析,重点关注影响青少年对 疫苗 犹豫不决的因素以及更广泛的公共卫生影响。
elements_zh.methods: 该评论采用综合健康信念模型 (HBM) 和 COM-B 理论框架,提出了一种文化敏感、基于证据的沟通策略,旨在解决 疫苗 的犹豫和错误信息。

title_zh: 通过公共卫生传播策略解决印度对 HPV 疫苗 的犹豫和错误信息。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT India witnessed a significant step forward in cervical cancer prevention and human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine coverage with the rollout of a nationwide free HPV vaccination drive aimed at vaccinating 14‐y‐old girls. However, the campaign’s success rate can be significantly reduced if timely measures to tackle vaccine hesitancy and related misinformation are not taken into account. This commentary article discusses the effects of HPV vaccine misinformation, identifies global vaccine hesitancy factors, and highlights behavioral determinants affecting HPV vaccine hesitancy and its coverage in India. It identifies low awareness, misconceptions, sociocultural beliefs, stigma, safety concerns, weak injunctive norms, parental resistance, urban–rural disparities, and health system barriers as key challenges associated with vaccine hesitancy and low vaccine uptake among adolescents in India. Using an integrated Health Belief Model (HBM) and COM-B theoretical framework, it proposes a culturally sensitive, evidence-based multifactorial communication strategy focused on raising awareness, building trust, countering misinformation, capacity building of healthcare providers, and enhancing opportunities for the adoption of HPV preventive behavior. The commentary highlights the need to actively engage parents, adolescents, healthcare providers, educators, influencers, media, and community members to strengthen vaccine confidence, social norms, and support India’s broader cervical cancer prevention goals in alignment with WHO’s 90–70–90 targets by 2030.
abstract_zh: 摘要 印度在 宫颈癌 预防和 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 覆盖方面取得了重大进展,在全国范围内推出了旨在为 14 岁女孩接种疫苗的免费 HPV 疫苗接种 活动。然而,如果不及时采取措施解决 疫苗 犹豫不决和相关错误信息的问题,该活动的成功率可能会大大降低。本文讨论了 HPV 疫苗 错误信息的影响,确定了全球 疫苗 犹豫因素,并重点介绍了影响 HPV 疫苗 犹豫及其在印度覆盖范围的行为决定因素。报告指出,印度青少年对 疫苗 犹豫不决和 疫苗 接受率低的关键挑战是认知度低、误解、社会文化信仰、耻辱、安全问题、禁令规范薄弱、父母抵制、城乡差异和卫生系统障碍。它利用综合的健康信念模型 (HBM) 和 COM-B 理论框架,提出了一种文化敏感、基于证据的多因素沟通策略,重点是提高认识、建立信任、反击错误信息、医疗保健提供者的能力建设以及增加采取 HPV 预防行为的机会。评论强调,需要积极吸引家长、青少年、医疗保健提供者、教育工作者、影响者、媒体和社区成员参与,以增强 疫苗 信心、社会规范,并支持印度更广泛的 疫苗 预防目标,与世界卫生组织到 2030 年实现 90-70-90 的目标保持一致。

title: When protein lactylation meets viral infection: A review.
abstract: Lactate is an important metabolic byproduct that regulates protein function under diverse physiological and pathological conditions. Protein lactylation has emerged as a critical regulatory mechanism in virus-host interactions. Lactylation reshapes the tRNA regulatory system during Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV) infection and modulates the mRNA processing machinery to regulate host antiviral immunity during severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) infection. In addition, lactylation also regulates telomere maintenance during human papillomavirus (HPV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) infections. Although an increasing number of studies has revealed have clarified the involvement of protein lactylation during viral infections, a systematic understanding of the interplay of lactylation between host immunity and viral evasion is currently lacking. Herein, we summarize the most recent advances and emerging discoveries regarding the role of protein lactylation in regulating host immunity and cellular responses to lactate during viral infections. We further discuss the mechanistic crosstalk between lactylation and other signaling networks, aiming to broaden the current perspective of lactylation-mediated regulation in viral pathogenesis, ultimately emphasizing this modification as an emerging target for antiviral interventions.

title_original: When protein lactylation meets viral infection: A review.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on the role of protein lactylation in regulating host immunity and cellular responses to lactate during human papillomavirus (HPV) infections, particularly in the context of HPV-associated diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia, HPV-associated cervical cancer, and HPV-associated anal cancer. The central question is how lactylation influences viral pathogenesis and immune responses.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of recent advances in understanding protein lactylation's role in viral infections. It does not report a systematic review or meta-analysis, but rather summarizes findings from various studies on lactylation and its interaction with viral infections, including HPV.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Protein lactylation modulates the tRNA regulatory system and mRNA processing machinery during HPV infection, thereby influencing host antiviral immunity. It also plays a role in telomere maintenance, which is critical for viral persistence and oncogenic transformation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while studies have clarified the involvement of lactylation in viral infections, a systematic understanding of the interplay between lactylation, host immunity, and viral evasion mechanisms remains lacking. This indicates a gap in the current evidence base.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for further research to elucidate the mechanistic crosstalk between lactylation and other signaling networks in the context of HPV infections. This could lead to the development of novel antiviral interventions targeting lactylation.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the emerging role of protein lactylation in modulating host immunity and cellular responses during human papillomavirus (HPV) infections. It highlights how lactylation influences the tRNA regulatory system and mRNA processing machinery, thereby affecting antiviral immunity and telomere maintenance. While recent studies have clarified lactylation's involvement in HPV-related processes, a comprehensive understanding of its interplay with host immunity and viral evasion remains lacking. The review suggests that further research into lactylation's mechanistic interactions could provide new insights into HPV pathogenesis and open avenues for antiviral interventions.

abstract_zh: 乳酸是一种重要的代谢副产物,在多种生理和病理条件下调节蛋白质功能。蛋白质乳酰化已成为病毒-宿主 相互作用中的关键调节机制。在卡波西肉瘤相关疱疹病毒 (KSHV) 感染期间,乳酰化重塑了 tRNA 调节系统,并在血小板减少综合征病毒 (SFTSV) 严重发烧期间调节 mRNA 加工机制来调节 宿主 抗病毒药物 免疫。此外,乳酰化还调节 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 和乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 感染期间的端粒维持。尽管越来越多的研究表明,已经阐明了病毒感染过程中蛋白质乳酰化的参与,但目前缺乏对 宿主 免疫和病毒逃避之间乳酰化相互作用的系统了解。在此,我们总结了有关蛋白质乳酰化在病毒感染期间调节 宿主 免疫和细胞对乳酸的反应中的作用的最新进展和新发现。我们进一步讨论了乳酰化与其他信号网络之间的机制串扰,旨在拓宽病毒 发病机制 中乳酰化介导的调节的当前视角,最终强调这种修饰作为 抗病毒药物 干预的新兴目标。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇综述是对理解蛋白质乳酰化在病毒感染中作用的最新进展的叙述性综合。它没有报告系统评价或荟萃分析,而是总结了有关乳酰化及其与病毒感染(包括 HPV)相互作用的各种研究的结果。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 蛋白质乳酰化在 HPV 感染过程中调节 tRNA 调节系统和 mRNA 加工机制,从而影响 宿主 抗病毒药物 免疫。它还在端粒维持中发挥作用,这对于病毒持久性和致癌转化至关重要。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该评论指出,虽然研究已经阐明了乳酰化在病毒感染中的参与,但仍然缺乏对乳酰化、宿主 免疫和病毒逃避机制之间相互作用的系统理解。这表明当前证据基础存在差距。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述强调需要进一步研究来阐明 HPV 感染背景下乳酰化和其他信号网络之间的机制串扰。这可能导致针对乳酰化的新型 抗病毒药物 干预措施的开发。

title: Maximizing Cytologic Specimen Supernatants: a New Player in the Molecular Toolbox.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple cytologic preparations are available to cytopathologists to use for molecular testing (MT). Proper use of each is necessary to improve patient outcomes. Residual cytology specimens and cytology specimen supernatants (CSS) are novel sources from which nucleic acid may be extracted for MT. CSS may be of particular interest to the cytology community, as it is routinely discarded. If repurposed for MT instead, it may allow pathologists to preserve cellular material from traditional preparations for other ancillary studies. SUMMARY: To evaluate the utility of CSS, it is first necessary to understand the metrics by which MT is evaluated. These include nucleic acid quantity and tumor percentage, the latter of which may be difficult to precisely quantify in CSS. Metrics of nucleic acid quantity include direct measures, such as degradation value (measure of nucleic acid fragmentation), and indirect measures, including many sequencing-derived metrics and concordance with formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue or cell blocks. Specimen contamination and turnaround time are also critical for patient care. Human papillomavirus testing on residual cytology specimens serves as a model of the clinical utility of MT. More recently, studies have examined both the analytic and clinical value of a broad range of MTs performed on CSS derived from both exfoliative and fine needle aspiration cytology specimens and from specimens collected with and without fixative. These studies have demonstrated that CSS contains both cellular (genomic) and cell-free nucleic acid, and that their great advantages lie in reductions in specimen contamination and improvements in turnaround time. Variations in nucleic acid quantity and quality among studies suggest that further specimen optimization is desirable as CSS becomes more widely adopted as a source of nucleic acid.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human papillomaviruses (HPV) and their associated diseases, specifically examining the utility of cytology specimen supernatants (CSS) as a source for molecular testing (MT). The central question is whether CSS can be effectively used for MT, considering factors like nucleic acid quantity, tumor percentage, and clinical relevance.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a broad range of studies that have analyzed the analytic and clinical value of molecular testing performed on CSS derived from various cytology specimens. The methods include evaluating nucleic acid quantity through direct and indirect measures, such as degradation value and sequencing-derived metrics, as well as comparing CSS results with formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue or cell blocks.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The studies demonstrate that CSS contains both cellular and cell-free nucleic acid, and that its use in molecular testing offers significant advantages, including reduced specimen contamination and improved turnaround time. These findings suggest that CSS could be a valuable resource for molecular testing in the context of HPV-related diseases.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Variations in nucleic acid quantity and quality among studies indicate that further optimization of CSS as a source for molecular testing is needed. Additionally, the review notes that tumor percentage in CSS may be difficult to precisely quantify, which could affect the reliability of certain diagnostic outcomes.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: There is a clear need for research to optimize CSS for molecular testing, particularly in terms of standardizing nucleic acid extraction and quantification methods. Furthermore, the clinical utility of CSS in HPV-related diagnostics should be explored further to determine its potential impact on patient care.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the potential of cytology specimen supernatants (CSS) as a novel source for molecular testing (MT) in the context of human papillomaviruses (HPV). It highlights the advantages of CSS, including reduced contamination and faster turnaround times, while noting variations in nucleic acid quantity and quality across studies. The review suggests that further research is needed to optimize CSS for MT and to assess its clinical utility in HPV-related diseases such as cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and HPV-associated cancers.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 及其相关疾病,特别检查细胞学标本上清液 (CSS) 作为分子检测 (MT) 来源的效用。核心问题是考虑到核酸数量、肿瘤百分比和临床相关性等因素,CSS是否可以有效地用于MT。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述基于广泛的研究,这些研究分析了对来自各种细胞学标本的 CSS 进行分子测试的分析和临床价值。这些方法包括通过直接和间接测量(例如降解值和测序衍生指标)评估核酸数量,以及将 CSS 结果与福尔马林固定、石蜡包埋的组织或细胞块进行比较。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 研究表明,CSS 含有细胞和无细胞核酸,其在分子检测中的使用具有显着的优势,包括减少样本污染和缩短周转时间。这些发现表明 CSS 可能成为 HPV 相关疾病分子检测的宝贵资源。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 研究之间核酸数量和质量的差异表明,需要进一步优化 CSS 作为分子检测的来源。此外,该评论指出,CSS 中的肿瘤百分比可能难以精确量化,这可能会影响某些诊断结果的可靠性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 显然需要进行研究来优化 CSS 以进行分子检测,特别是在标准化核酸提取和定量方法方面。此外,应进一步探索 CSS 在 HPV 相关诊断中的临床效用,以确定其对患者护理的潜在影响。

abstract_zh: 背景:细胞病理学家可以使用多种细胞学制剂进行分子检测(MT)。正确使用每种药物对于改善患者的治疗效果是必要的。残留细胞学标本和细胞学标本上清液 (CSS) 是可提取核酸用于 MT 的新来源。CSS 可能对细胞学界特别感兴趣,因为它经常被丢弃。如果重新用于 MT,它可能允许病理学家保留传统制剂中的细胞材料,用于其他辅助研究。摘要:要评估 CSS 的实用性,首先需要了解评估 MT 的指标。其中包括核酸数量和肿瘤百分比,后者可能很难在 CSS 中精确量化。核酸数量的度量包括直接测量,例如降解值(核酸片段化的测量)和间接测量,包括许多测序衍生的度量以及与福尔马林固定、石蜡包埋的组织或细胞块的一致性。样本污染和周转时间对于患者护理也至关重要。人乳头瘤病毒 对残留细胞学标本的检测可作为 MT 临床应用的模型。最近,研究检验了对来自剥脱性和细针抽吸细胞学标本以及使用和不使用固定剂收集的标本的 CSS 进行的广泛 MT 的分析和临床价值。这些研究表明,CSS 含有细胞(基因组)和无细胞核酸,其巨大优势在于减少样本污染和缩短周转时间。研究中核酸数量和质量的差异表明,随着 CSS 被更广泛地用作核酸来源,需要进一步优化样本。

title: Modelling the impact of awareness campaigns on HPV transmission dynamics: a neural network-enhanced mathematical model.
abstract: HPV is the most common sexually transmitted infection; most sexually active individuals are exposed to HPV at some point in their lives, and the majority of these infections resolve naturally through the immune system. However, persistent infection with high-risk HPV types is the leading cause of cervical cancer worldwide, underscoring the importance of vaccination and early detection in reducing disease burden. In this study, the effect of an awareness campaign on the dynamics of human papillomavirus infection has been investigated through a mathematical model using neural networks. The basic characteristic, boundedness, the endemic and disease-free equilibrium point, and the reproduction number of the model have been investigated. Using the reproduction number, the stability of the model is also investigated. Moreover, a sensitivity analysis is performed to identify the most sensitive parameter affecting the spread and control of HPV. The deterministic numerical solution of the HPV transmission model was first obtained using the ode45 solver based on the Runge-Kutta method; the resulting solution trajectories were then used as training data for a feedforward neural network, which serves as a surrogate approximation model to validate and reproduce the system dynamics. The numerical simulation examines mean square error, validation performance, gradient, and mu across varying levels of vaccination coverage, public awareness, and cervical infection rates. Numerical simulation suggests that vaccination and awareness about the risk of human papillomavirus infection play a crucial role in controlling the spread of the virus in the population.

title: Application of an extended information-motivation-behavioral skills model to predict HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men.
abstract: Background: Human papillomavirus (HPV) causes substantial disease burden among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM), yet HPV vaccination pathways for men remain evolving in mainland China. Purpose: To apply a culturally adapted, extended Information-Motivation-Behavioral Skills (IMB) model to identify psychosocial pathways associated with HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese GBMSM. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted between December 2024 and January 2025 among 1,045 GBMSM living in mainland China. Measures included HPV-related information, health beliefs, anticipated regret, subjective norms, self-efficacy, and HPV vaccine acceptability. Measurement and structural equation models estimated direct and indirect pathways. Results: HPV vaccine acceptability was moderate (mean 3.40, SD 1.14). Subjective norms were the strongest predictor of acceptability (β = 0.68, p < .001), with additional positive effects from health beliefs (β = 0.17, p < .01), information (β = 0.14, p < .001), and self-efficacy (β = 0.13, p = .02). Anticipated regret showed a positive indirect effect through self-efficacy (unstandardized B = 0.056, 95% CI 0.01 to 0.12) but a negative direct association with acceptability (β = -0.11, p = .03). Conclusions: HPV vaccine acceptability among Chinese GBMSM was shaped predominantly by social norms, with self-efficacy acting as a key pathway through which psychosocial factors were associated with acceptability.

title: Single-cell transcriptomics uncovers HPV-driven immune evasion and establishes a TAB2-based prognostic signature in cervical cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a key driver in cervical cancer, yet the molecular mechanisms linking HPV to immune escape remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, and clinical data to analyze cervical cancer heterogeneity. scRNA-seq, inferCNV, and pseudotime analysis characterized HPV-associated cellular features and malignant transformation. hdWGCNA identified core gene modules. Univariate Cox, Lasso, and multivariate Cox regressions were used to construct a prognostic risk model. In vitro functional validation of TAB2 was also performed. RESULTS: Eleven major cell populations were identified, with epithelial cells as primary HPV targets. HPV-related gene enrichment increased with disease progression. Malignant cells exhibited significantly higher immune escape scores than non-tumor cells, strongly correlating with HPV infection levels (P < 0.001). hdWGCNA identified three modules linked to immunosuppression, stress response, and proliferation. An eight-gene risk model showed stable prognostic performance across TCGA and GEO cohorts, served as an independent prognostic factor (P < 0.05), and correlated with WNT/TGFβ pathway activation and immune checkpoint genes. TAB2 knockdown significantly suppressed cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. CONCLUSION: This multi-omics analysis identifies transcriptional programs associated with HPV infection and immune escape in cervical cancer. The eight-gene risk model shows potential for prognosis prediction and patient stratification, offering a theoretical basis for individualized treatment. The mechanistic hypotheses generated warrant further experimental validation.

source_records.abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a key driver in cervical cancer, yet the molecular mechanisms linking HPV to immune escape remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), bulk transcriptome, and clinical data to analyze cervical cancer heterogeneity. scRNA-seq, inferCNV, and pseudotime analysis characterized HPV-associated cellular features and malignant transformation. hdWGCNA identified core gene modules. Univariate Cox, Lasso, and multivariate Cox regressions were used to construct a prognostic risk model. In vitro functional validation of TAB2 was also performed. RESULTS: Eleven major cell populations were identified, with epithelial cells as primary HPV targets. HPV-related gene enrichment increased with disease progression. Malignant cells exhibited significantly higher immune escape scores than non-tumor cells, strongly correlating with HPV infection levels (P < 0.001). hdWGCNA identified three modules linked to immunosuppression, stress response, and proliferation. An eight-gene risk model showed stable prognostic performance across TCGA and GEO cohorts, served as an independent prognostic factor (P < 0.05), and correlated with WNT/TGFβ pathway activation and immune checkpoint genes. TAB2 knockdown significantly suppressed cervical cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro. CONCLUSION: This multi-omics analysis identifies transcriptional programs associated with HPV infection and immune escape in cervical cancer. The eight-gene risk model shows potential for prognosis prediction and patient stratification, offering a theoretical basis for individualized treatment. The mechanistic hypotheses generated warrant further experimental validation.

title: Global Lip and Oral Cavity Cancer: Analysis of the 2021 Global Burden of Disease Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION AND AIMS: This study aimed to use the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 Study to analyse the trends in the disease burden of lip and oral cavity cancer (LOCC) at the global, regional, and national levels (1990-2021); to quantify the impacts of population growth, aging, and epidemiological changes on incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs); assess health inequalities associated with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) across countries; and predict the burden trends up to 2050 based on the Bayesian age-period-cohort model (BAPC) model. METHODS: Data from the GBD 2021 Study were included in the age-period-cohort (APC) model to evaluate the effects of age, period, and cohort. Decomposition analysis was used to determine the influencing factors. RESULTS: The global burden of LOCC showed a 'high north, heavy south' bimodal distribution with significant sex differences. Decomposition analyses indicated aging and population growth drive increased morbidity and prevalence, whereas epidemiological changes reduce mortality and DALYs. Absolute inequalities measured using the slope index of inequality (SII) revealed indicating persistent SDI-related absolute inequalities. Concurrently, the concentration index (CI) showed that prevalence remained concentrated in high-SDI settings (CI: 0.26-0.13), whereas mortality and DALYs became increasingly concentrated in low-SDI settings. Projections to 2050 show upward trends in age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR), age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALYs rate (ASDR). CONCLUSION: Global LOCC showed increasing incidence and prevalence alongside declining mortality and DALYs from 1990 to 2021, with higher burden in males. Population aging and prevalence increases, whereas epidemiological changes mitigated mortality. BAPC projections indicate increases across all indicators by 2050. SDI-stratified strategies are required: human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and screening for high-SDI regions; tobacco control for middle-SDI regions; betel quid regulation and primary care investment for low-SDI regions; and ultraviolet (UV) protection for lip cancer hotspots. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

title_zh: 全球唇癌和口腔癌:2021 年全球疾病负担研究分析。
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION AND AIMS: This study aimed to use the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 Study to analyse the trends in the disease burden of lip and oral cavity cancer (LOCC) at the global, regional, and national levels (1990-2021); to quantify the impacts of population growth, aging, and epidemiological changes on incidence, prevalence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs); assess health inequalities associated with the Socio-demographic Index (SDI) across countries; and predict the burden trends up to 2050 based on the Bayesian age-period-cohort model (BAPC) model. METHODS: Data from the GBD 2021 Study were included in the age-period-cohort (APC) model to evaluate the effects of age, period, and cohort. Decomposition analysis was used to determine the influencing factors. RESULTS: The global burden of LOCC showed a 'high north, heavy south' bimodal distribution with significant sex differences. Decomposition analyses indicated aging and population growth drive increased morbidity and prevalence, whereas epidemiological changes reduce mortality and DALYs. Absolute inequalities measured using the slope index of inequality (SII) revealed indicating persistent SDI-related absolute inequalities. Concurrently, the concentration index (CI) showed that prevalence remained concentrated in high-SDI settings (CI: 0.26-0.13), whereas mortality and DALYs became increasingly concentrated in low-SDI settings. Projections to 2050 show upward trends in age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR), age-standardized prevalence rate (ASPR), age-standardized mortality rate (ASMR), and age-standardized DALYs rate (ASDR). CONCLUSION: Global LOCC showed increasing incidence and prevalence alongside declining mortality and DALYs from 1990 to 2021, with higher burden in males. Population aging and prevalence increases, whereas epidemiological changes mitigated mortality. BAPC projections indicate increases across all indicators by 2050. SDI-stratified strategies are required: human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination and screening for high-SDI regions; tobacco control for middle-SDI regions; betel quid regulation and primary care investment for low-SDI regions; and ultraviolet (UV) protection for lip cancer hotspots. abstract_zh: 简介和目的:本研究旨在利用2021年全球疾病负担(GBD)研究来分析全球、区域和国家层面(1990-2021年)唇癌和口腔癌(LOCC)疾病负担的趋势;量化人口增长、老龄化和流行病学变化对 发病率、患病率、死亡率 和伤残调整生命年 (DALY) 的影响;评估各国与社会人口指数(SDI)相关的健康不平等;并基于贝叶斯年龄周期-队列研究模型(BAPC)模型预测到2050年的负担趋势。方法:GBD 2021 研究的数据纳入年龄-周期-队列研究 (APC) 模型,以评估年龄、周期和 队列研究 的影响。采用分解分析法确定影响因素。结果:全球 LOCC 负担呈现“北高南重”的双峰分布,且性别差异显着。分解分析表明,老龄化和人口增长导致发病率和 患病率 增加,而流行病学变化则降低 死亡率 和 DALY。使用不平等斜率指数 (SII) 测量的绝对不平等表明,与 SDI 相关的绝对不平等持续存在。同时,集中指数 (CI) 显示 患病率 仍然集中在高 SDI 设置中(CI:0.26-0.13),而 死亡率 和 DALY 则越来越集中在低 SDI 设置中。到 2050 年的预测显示,年龄标准化 发病率 率 (ASIR)、年龄标准化 患病率 率 (ASPR)、年龄标准化 死亡率 率 (ASMR) 和年龄标准化 DALY 率 (ASDR) 呈上升趋势。结论:从 1990 年到 2021 年,全球 LOCC 显示 发病率 和 患病率 增加,同时 死亡率 和 DALY 下降,其中男性负担更高。人口老龄化和 患病率 增加,而流行病学变化则减轻 死亡率。BAPC 预测表明,到 2050 年,所有指标都会有所增加。需要 SDI 分层策略:人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗接种 和高 SDI 区域的筛查;SDI 中部地区的烟草控制;对低 SDI 地区的槟榔液监管和初级保健投资;以及针对唇癌热点的紫外线 (UV) 防护。临床试验编号:不适用。

title: HPV Vaccination Predictors Among College Students
abstract: College students remain at increased risk for acquiring human papillomavirus (HPV), yet HPV vaccination coverage remains suboptimal despite the availability of a safe and effective vaccine. This study examined predictors of HPV vaccination and HPV- and HPV vaccine-related knowledge, beliefs, and hesitancy among undergraduate students at a southern United States university. An online cross-sectional survey was administered to undergraduate students aged 18-26 years in November 2024. Descriptive statistics summarized participant characteristics, vaccination status, and HPV-related measures. Multinomial logistic regression models were used to examine factors associated with HPV vaccination status while estimating adjusted odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 1,127 respondents (mean age, 20.1 years), most were female (74.1%), White (74.9%), and insured (90.4%). Overall, 48.4% reported receiving at least one dose of the HPV vaccine, with only 21.7% completion. More than 30% were unsure of their HPV vaccination status. HPV knowledge, HPV vaccine knowledge and beliefs, and vaccine hesitancy were all independently associated with vaccination status (all p < 0.001). Participants with stronger positive HPV vaccine beliefs and lower vaccine hesitancy had significantly greater odds of reporting HPV vaccination. In secondary analyses, both provider and parental recommendation were significantly associated with younger age at initiation. HPV vaccination initiation and completion remain low among college students, with substantial gaps in knowledge, awareness, and confidence. College campuses represent an important setting for interventions that improve HPV-related knowledge, strengthen vaccine confidence, increase awareness of personal vaccination status, and promote vaccination to reduce future HPV-associated cancers.

title: Preclinical Evaluation of Chemoradiation Resistance Using 18F-FDG PET/CT in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
abstract: Purpose: There is an urgent need for improved prognostic tools and biological understanding of chemoradiation resistance in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This study established a preclinical imaging dataset aimed at identifying prognostic imaging features from 18F-FDG micro-PET/CT scans in HNSCC mouse models. Methods: Three orthotopic murine models were utilized: two human papillomavirus (HPV)-negative (MOC1, MOC2) and one HPV-positive (MLM1). When tumor volume exceeded 50 mm^3, chemoradiation was initiated using cisplatin (5 mg/kg) and image-guided radiation therapy (8 Gy) on days 0 and 7. 18F-FDG micro-PET/CT imaging was performed on day 14. Tumors were manually segmented on PET/CT, and quantitative image features including tumor volume, SUVmean, and SUVmax were extracted. Treatment response was evaluated by relative tumor size on day 11 compared to day 0. Tumor growth and survival were compared across models using multiple-effects model and log-rank. Imaging feature associations were evaluated by Mann-Whitney U tests. Associations between survival, SUVmax, and tumor volume were assessed using Cox proportional hazards modeling and Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing. Results: A total of 121 mice were treated and imaged. title: Systematic Workflow Optimization for Ultra-Sensitive Targeted Immunopeptidomics.
abstract: Epitope detection sensitivity remains a primary bottleneck in mass spectrometry (MS)-based immunopeptidomics, as conventional discovery-based workflows such as data-dependent (DDA) and data-independent acquisition (DIA) frequently lack the sensitivity required to detect ultra-low abundant targets. While these untargeted methods are powerful for mapping the general immunopeptidome, the stochastic nature of precursor selection and the presence of complex, chimeric spectra mean that rare species, such as viral or mutation-derived neoepitopes, often remain undetected. In this study, we present optiPRM+, an ultra-sensitive targeted-first workflow for the Orbitrap Exploris 480 platform that integrates systematically optimized targeted acquisition with untargeted DIA contextualization to bridge this sensitivity gap. Our approach centers on the empirical characterization of target peptides using direct infusion-MS to determine optimal fragmentation conditions and inclusion list-driven data-dependent acquisition (iDDA). To maximize signal-to-noise ratios for these trace-level targets, we employed ultra-high MS2 resolutions (up to 480,000), ion injection times up to 1000 ms, and narrow precursor isolation windows. Additionally, we discovered that precursors with a charge state exceeding their basic amino acid count require unusually low energies for optimal fragmentation, which is especially relevant for the non-tryptic peptides characteristic of the immunopeptidome. We applied the optiPRM+ workflow to the challenging biological case of Human Papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16), a virus known to suppress antigen presentation pathways. This optimized strategy enabled the confident identification and validation of the human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-A*02:01-restricted epitope TIHDIILECV and, to our knowledge, the first MS-based detection of two novel viral targets: ISEYRHYCY (HLA-A*01:01) and CVYCKQQLLR (HLA-A*11:01). Subsequent global immunopeptidome analysis via DIA confirmed that these ultra-low abundance peptides were not detectable through untargeted methods despite being clearly validated by our targeted approach. By successfully detecting these viral peptides, we demonstrate that a systematically optimized targeted-first approach can uncover biologically relevant epitopes that remain invisible to conventional discovery-based workflows.

title: Extended HPV Genotyping for Risk Stratification in Cervical Screening: A Population-based Study
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Population-based data on extended HPV genotyping for risk stratification in routine cervical cancer screening are limited. We evaluated the association between oncogenic risk categories derived from extended HPV genotyping and cervical screening outcomes (cytology and histology) in a large population-based cohort (October 2021-September 2023). METHODS: This retrospective observational study analyzed HPV results and corresponding cytology and histology from screened women between October 2021 and September 2023. High-risk HPV genotypes were classified into three mutually exclusive categories: high (HOT), moderate (MOT), and low (LOT), developed for the organizational framework of this particular study. Cytologic and histologic outcomes were compared across categories using chi-square tests, and PPVs for CIN2+ and CIN3+ were calculated. RESULTS: Among 448,394 screened women, overall HPV prevalence was 8.6%. HOT, MOT, and LOT genotypes accounted for 35.5%, 24.0%, and 40.5% of HPV-positive infections, respectively. Cytologic severity differed significantly across oncogenic risk categories (p<.0001), with HOT genotypes contributing disproportionately to high-grade cytologic abnormalities. Histologic follow-up demonstrated marked differences in disease severity, with HOT genotypes accounting for 68.8% of CIN3+ diagnoses compared with 19.7% for MOT and 11.5% for LOT. title: Giant anogenital condyloma acuminata with extragenital involvement in an immunocompetent host.
abstract: Condyloma acuminata is an uncommon epithelial proliferative and infiltrative growth associated with human papillomavirus (HPV) subtypes 6 and 11. Giant condyloma acuminata is a more aggressive variant characterised by extensive growth, anatomical disfigurement, psychosocial morbidity and a high recurrence rate. Extragenital involvement in an immunocompetent individual is uncommonly reported in the literature. We report a case of an immunocompetent young woman who developed a rapidly progressive verrucous growth involving the vulva, lower vagina, perianal region and also extragenital sites (inframammary fold and axilla). Pelvic MRI demonstrated a large exophytic lesion without underlying stromal involvement. Complete surgical excision with histopathological confirmation demonstrated condyloma acuminata with low-risk HPV type 11. Early recurrence occurred within 3 months, which was managed by topical medication. This case highlights the importance of clinical examination, the role of MRI followed by surgical excision with long-term follow-up even in immunocompetent patients.

abstract: Cancers containing histologically distinct cell populations could arise from multiple transforming events, from transdifferentiation late in tumor evolution, or from a single progenitor cell. title: Proteomic Profiling of Exosomes from HPV-Positive and HPV-Negative Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Selective Cargo Packaging.
abstract: Oncogenic viruses, such as human papillomavirus (HPV), alter the endosomal system to manipulate the proteomic content of extracellular vesicles, aiding their persistence and disease progression. HPV has emerged as a key risk factor for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). However, the influence of HPV on the exosomal proteomics remains poorly understood. Label-free quantitative proteomics was employed to analyze proteins extracted from HPV16-positive (93VU147T, UDSCC2) and HPV-negative (OCT1) HNSCC cell lines and their exosomes. Data are available via ProteomeXchange with identifier PXD067001. PCA revealed distinct clustering of HPV16-positive and -negative cells and exosomes. Differential expression analysis revealed 130 and 136 DEPs in exosomes of 93VU147T and UDSCC2, respectively, and 326 and 320 DEPs in the corresponding cells. Gene Ontology enrichment showed that HPV16-positive exosomal proteins and cells were associated mainly with protein digestion and absorption, different neurodegenerative diseases, and PI3K/Akt signaling. Exosomes showed distinct profiling from that of parental cells, emphasizing selective cargo packaging. Overall, the study demonstrates that HPV modulates the exosomal content in HNSCC, suggesting potential implications in tumor progression and biomarker discovery.

title: Reconfiguring scientific competition: patent consolidation and the access politics of the HPV vaccine
abstract: Abstract The invention of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine occurred at a moment when academic life science research was becoming increasingly reoriented toward market-driven goals. This transformation, shaped by policy shifts promoting the commercialisation of academic research, altered traditional forms of scientific competition. Economic value came to structure not only research agendas but also the institutional logic of academic practice. Intellectual property rights played a key role in materialising this shift, with powerful market actors influencing the outcomes of scientific contests to secure monopolistic control. The case of the HPV vaccine illustrates how upstream innovation processes, especially decisions about ownership, licensing, and legal structuring, determine downstream outcomes such as pricing and access. This challenges prevailing approaches in public health that treat access inequalities as isolated or downstream issues, instead highlighting how the architecture of biomedical innovation itself shapes the terms of inclusion and exclusion in global health.

title: HPV prevention awareness, vaccination willingness, and vaccine-related perceptions among middle-school girls in three Arab countries: an exploratory online survey
abstract: Background Cervical cancer is largely preventable through human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, screening, and timely treatment; however, adolescent HPV literacy remains inconsistent. Egypt, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates have different publicly documented HPV-vaccination and cervical-screening contexts. This study explored HPV and cervical cancer prevention awareness, selected Health Belief Model-informed beliefs, vaccination willingness, and vaccine-related perceptions among middle-school girls in these countries. Methods An exploratory online cross-sectional survey was conducted among 300 students, with equal quota-like groups of 100 per country recruited through non-probability snowball sampling. Analyses were primarily descriptive; one complete-case exploratory logistic model examined factors associated with willingness to accept free HPV vaccination. Results Overall, 89/300 participants (29.7%) had heard of HPV, 103/300 (34.3%) had heard of cervical cancer, and 49/300 (16.3%) were aware of cervical screening. School nurses were the most frequently reported HPV information source among source-item respondents (47/90; 52.2%). HPV-vaccine awareness was reported by 131/298 participants (44.0%), previous vaccination by 106/300 (35.3%), and willingness to accept free vaccination by 197/300 (65.7%). Responses to five negatively worded vaccine-perception items were predominantly neutral or reflected disagreement rather than consistent endorsement of distrust. The exploratory model generated several inverse associations with willingness, but these estimates are sample-specific and hypothesis-generating. Conclusion Prevention awareness was limited despite relatively high stated willingness to accept free vaccination. The findings support culturally adapted, school-linked education and representative studies using validated measures, parent-linked information, and verified vaccination records.

title: Closing the Cervical Cancer Gap: Integrating HPV Genotyping, Cervical Dysplasia Screening, Vaccination, and Community Awareness in Eastern Kenya
abstract: In 2023, cervical cancer was the fourth most common type of cancer among women, with over 600,000 new cases and 340,000 deaths globally. Approximately 90% of the mortality cases occur in low and middle-income (LMIC) countries, especially in Sub-Saharan Africa. It is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women in Kenya. Cervical cancer is caused by human papillomavirus (HPV) infection. There are over 200 HPV genotypes, which are classified as high- and low-risk HPVs. This chapter explores how integrating HPV genotyping, cervical dysplasia detection, screening, vaccination, and community awareness can help close the cervical cancer gap in Eastern Kenya. In this study, 317 women – 161 HIV-infected (161) and 156 non-infected—aged 18–46 years (mean age: 34.3, SD ± 10.4) were recruited from Eastern Kenya. HIV-positive women had higher rates of both high- and low-risk HPV type infections, with HPV81, a non-vaccine type, being linked to cervical dysplasia. A higher primary diagnostic accuracy was established by human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA polymerase chain reaction (PCR). HIV-infected women also showed increased specificity through both primary and triage testing approaches. The literature review highlights distinct region-specific challenges and the disproportionate burden of non-vaccine HPV types in other regions. This study reviews how low awareness, poor screening uptake, and persistent misconceptions contribute to late cervical dysplasia diagnosis and poor screening outcomes. This study highlights the need for Eastern Kenya-specific vaccination, culturally sensitive awareness, and molecular diagnostics to accelerate cervical cancer elimination.
authors: Lucy M. Kamau and Raphael Lwembe
journal: Advances in Cervical Cancer - Diagnostic and Therapeutic Considerations [Working Title]

title: PAX1 and ZNF582 Methylation as a Triage Strategy in Cytologic and hrHPV+ Scrapings in Both Chinese and Dutch Cohorts.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The methylation of paired boxed gene 1 (PAX1) and zinc finger protein 582 (ZNF582) has been proved to have good diagnostic efficacy to detect cervical precancerous lesions in Asian populations, but their performance in Dutch populations is still unclear. We assessed PAX1 and ZNF582 methylation in both Dutch and Chinese cohorts. METHODS: Cervical scrapings were evaluated from 2 independent groups. The Dutch cohort (population-based screening) provided 190 abnormal cytology scrapings, and 138 cases tested positive for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV). The hospital-based Chinese cohort included 246 specimens (205 abnormal cytology and 227 hrHPV+). Quantitative methylation-specific PCR was employed to analyze methylation. RESULTS: PAX1 and ZNF582 methylation showed high specificity of 91% to 97% with moderate sensitivity of 43% to 61% for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) 2 or worse (CIN2+) in abnormal cytology and hrHPV+ samples in both cohorts. Sensitivity for CIN3+ increased to 55% to 86% but with lower specificity (85%-93%). For detecting CIN2+, PAX1/ZNF582 methylation performed similarly in Dutch and Chinese cohorts. However, for CIN3+, the Chinese cohort showed significantly higher sensitivity, with comparable specificity. We also evaluated combining these genes with our established markers (C13ORF18, JAM3, and ZSCAN1). The best diagnostic performance was achieved by combining PAX1 or ZNF582 with JAM3 in the Dutch cohort. CONCLUSIONS: In conclusion, regardless of race or geography, methylation of PAX1 or ZNF582 is highly specific for detecting CIN2+/CIN3+ lesions in hrHPV+ or cytologically abnormal scrapings. Triage testing using these markers might significantly reduce immediate colposcopies. IMPACT: PAX1/ZNF582 methylation triage for cytology+/hrHPV+ scrapings may reduce immediate colposcopies.
authors: Ate G J van der Zee

title: Awareness and Knowledge Levels of Cervical Cancer and HPV and Attitudes Toward HPV Vaccination in Algeria
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cervical cancer (CC), mainly caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), is one of the major cancers threatening women’s health in Algeria. However, despite the existence of a cost-effective vaccine, it has not yet been introduced into the national vaccination program. Recent information indicated that its introduction will be imminent. Thus, the current study was conducted to evaluate the level of awareness and knowledge about CC and HPV among the Algerian population as well as its attitudes toward HPV vaccination. Methods: A cross-sectional survey was carried out between 4 November 2022 and 8 May 2023 using a self-administered questionnaire that was diffused through social media platforms. Results: A total of 414 participants were included in our sample, with the dominance of those aged 18 to 30 years old (74.6%), those with university education (75.8%), and those with a medium financial level (77.5%). A high level of awareness was reported (76.3%), especially among healthcare workers (98.4%, OR: 17.099, 95% CI: 2.294–127.476, sig. = 0.06), participants aged more than 30 years (87.6%, OR: 2.78, 95% CI: 1.313–5.883, sig. = 0.008), and females (85.1%, OR: 2.02, 95% CI: 1.15–3.548, sig. However, the level of knowledge did not follow, since less than a third (32.1%) of the participants only were aware of HPV, and multiple gaps were reported regarding its epidemiology and its prevention. Moreover, while 30.8% of the participants were willing to get the HPV vaccine, 40.5% were hesitant, and 27.7% were resistant. The causes of rejection/hesitancy included mainly complacency, vaccine refusal, and the lack of confidence in the vaccine. In addition, hesitant and reluctant participants have shown a low level of knowledge and a high score of conspiracy beliefs. Conclusions: These results provide new insights into knowledge and attitudes towards CC and HPV vaccination. It reported that despite the high level of awareness about CC, gaps of knowledge remain and vaccination hesitancy/reluctance is persistent. These results suggest the need for raising awareness particularly about HPV which will consequently help to increase HPV vaccine acceptance.

title: Machine learning-enabled smartphone CRISPR-Cas12a lateral flow platform for sensitive detection of circulating HPV DNA.
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) is a major cause of cervical cancer, and improved point-of-care (POC) detection is critical for early intervention. Although PCR-based assays are highly sensitive, their reliance on centralized laboratory infrastructure limits accessibility in decentralized settings. CRISPR-Cas diagnostics combined with lateral flow assays (LFA) offer a rapid alternative; however, visual interpretation of faint test bands remains subjective and variable. Here, we developed a smartphone-based CRISPR-Cas12a LFA platform integrated with an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework for quantitative detection of circulating HPV DNA in plasma. Standardized image acquisition was implemented using a light-controlled enclosure, and radiomics-inspired features were analyzed using a multivariable logistic regression model. The system was trained on 150 plasma samples and validated in an independent cohort of 60 samples. The optimized model achieved 96.7% sensitivity and 100% specificity, outperforming visual interpretation, particularly for low-signal samples. Performance remained stable across different smartphone models, lighting conditions, and operators, with rapid on-device inference enabling consistent and reliable operation. This integrated CRISPR-LFA platform demonstrates accurate and reproducible detection of circulating HPV DNA and supports feasibility for POC applications, pending further validation in broader clinical settings.

title: Beyond the hallmarks of cancer: enabling technologies reshaping cancer diagnosis, prevention, and treatment
abstract: Cancer biology has been organized for 2 decades by the hallmarks framework, articulated in 2000 and most recently revised in 2026. The pace of technological change in oncology now requires reframing how cancer is detected, prevented, and treated. This review argues that the hallmarks framework, while historically essential, is no longer sufficient on its own to capture contemporary cancer care, and repositions the discussion around enabling technologies that operate across and beyond individual hallmarks. For diagnosis, multi-omic liquid biopsy, AI-assisted radiomics and digital pathology, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell sequencing, and machine-learning analysis of plasma proteomics now support earlier detection, prediction of cancer risk years before diagnosis, monitoring of clonal evolution, and prediction of treatment response. For prevention, the validated population-level success of Human papillomavirus and HBV vaccination is contrasted with investigational directions including mRNA platforms, CRISPR-enabled antigen optimization, personalized neoantigen prophylaxis, and biomarker-stratified molecular interception, none of which has yet been validated in prospective human cancer-prevention trials. For treatment, the discussion is organized by modality class: immune checkpoint inhibitors and resistance strategies, antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific antibodies and T-cell engagers, radioligand therapies, tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy, CRISPR-edited CAR-T and TCR therapies, photonic and photoimmunologic therapies, RNA therapeutics, and adaptive combination regimens. Comparative tables summarize diagnostic platforms, immunotherapeutic modalities, photonic therapies, CRISPR-edited immunotherapy trials, neoantigen vaccine pipelines, and convergent strategies. The trajectory of oncology will be defined less by incremental refinement of hallmarks and more by convergent technologies that integrate diagnostics, prevention, and treatment into continuous, data-driven systems.

title: An In-House PCR-RFLP Workflow for HPV Genotyping: Proof-of-Concept and Preliminary Rea-gent-Cost Analysis in Ecuador
abstract: Human Papillomaviruses (HPV) account for approximately 90% of cervical cancer cases worldwide. While the World Health Organization has set ambitious goals for the elimination of cervical cancer through early screening, the high cost of proprietary commercial molecular tests severely restricts access for vulnerable populations in low- and middle-income countries. Twelve cervical samples were processed, of which two tested positive for HPV. One positive sample was analyzed as a proof of concept for the workflow, demonstrating a highly affordable alternative to commercial assays. Although further validation with a larger sample set and confirmation using an independent reference method are required, the implementation of frugal strategies throughout the sample processing workflow, combined with the use of existing laboratory infrastructure and personnel, reduced the estimated direct reagent cost of genotyping up to 49 HPV types to approximately US$17 per sample. Implementing this underutilized diagnostic approach in public-sector laboratories could significantly expand cervical cancer screening programs in developing countries. Ultimately, this framework serves as a scalable blueprint to advance health equity and diagnostic sovereignty across Latin America and the Global South, with the potential to expand access to HPV screening for low-income women, who currently bear the highest burden of cervical cancer mortality.
